snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ SSC Reasoning Hook: Tree symbols: +: Male, -: Female, : : Couple. North-South-East-West. Pythagoras for distance. Generation gap: Vertical.

quick_notes.title: Blood Relation Symbols
quick_notes.explanation: In blood relation problems, we use symbols to represent family members. A plus sign (+) means a male person, and a minus sign (-) means a female person. A colon (:) shows a married couple, like a husband and wife. The vertical bar (|) indicates a generation gap, meaning a parent and child relationship. A horizontal dash (-) between two people means they are siblings, brothers or sisters. These symbols help us quickly draw and understand family trees.

quick_notes.title: Relationships
quick_notes.detail: Maternal (Mother's side), Paternal (Father's side). Brother-in-law, Sister-in-law, Cousin.
quick_notes.explanation: Your family has two sides: your mother's side is called maternal, and your father's side is called paternal. A brother-in-law is the brother of your spouse, or the husband of your sister. A sister-in-law is the sister of your spouse, or the wife of your brother. A cousin is the child of your aunt or uncle, meaning you share grandparents with that person. For example, your mother's sister's daughter is your cousin on the maternal side. Remember that all these relationships are based on blood or marriage connections.

quick_notes.title: Direction Sense
quick_notes.detail: Standard Map: North (Up), South (Down), East (Right), West (Left).
quick_notes.explanation: Direction Sense is the skill of understanding and following directions using the four main cardinal directions: North (N), South (S), East (E), and West (W). On a standard map, North is always at the top, South at the bottom, East to the right, and West to the left. For example, if you face North, your right side is East, your left side is West, and behind you is South. These four directions are fixed relative to the Earth, meaning North always points toward the geographic North Pole, regardless of where you stand. To solve direction problems, imagine yourself standing at a starting point and moving step by step according to the given turns or distances.

quick_notes.title: Turns
quick_notes.detail: Clockwise (Right), Anti-clockwise (Left). A 90° right turn from North is East.
quick_notes.explanation: When we talk about turns, clockwise means turning in the same direction as the hands of a clock move, which is also called a right turn. Anti-clockwise, also called counterclockwise or a left turn, is the opposite direction, like the hands moving backwards. For example, if you are facing North and make a 90-degree right turn (clockwise), you will then be facing East. A 90-degree turn means you rotate a quarter of a full circle.

quick_notes.title: Shortest Distance
quick_notes.detail: Usually forms a right-angled triangle. Use sqrt(a^2 + b^2). (Pythagoras).
quick_notes.explanation: The shortest distance between two points is a straight line, and when you need to find that distance on a flat surface, you can often use a right-angled triangle. A right-angled triangle is a shape with three sides where one corner is a perfect 90-degree angle, like the corner of a square. The Pythagorean theorem, named after the ancient mathematician Pythagoras, says that for this kind of triangle, the longest side opposite the right angle has a special relationship to the other two sides. To find the shortest distance, you treat the two known distances as the two shorter sides, which are called legs, and you use the formula square root of a squared plus b squared, written as sqrt(a^2 + b^2). In this formula, a and b are the lengths of the two legs, and the square root symbol means you find the number which, when multiplied by itself, gives the result of adding a squared and b squared together.
